public_rationale: The September 26, 2023 survey describes task decomposition, debate, human-feedback methods and interpretability alongside Constitutional AI [e7]. This establishes that alternatives existed before the claim, but does not settle whether there were “few” [e7]. A verdict would require an added rule defining a distinct “idea,” what qualifies as “on the table,” and how many count as “few.” Those choices would determine the assessment.
limitations: The survey does not supply a counting standard that can settle the claim.
Listing approaches does not establish their effectiveness or whether they offer comprehensive safety comparable to Constitutional AI.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Apart from Constitutional AI, few other AI safety ideas are seriously being proposed.

statement.excerpt: Few other ideas are even on the table.
statement.document_title: A CERN for AI and the Global Governance of AI

our_interpretation: The context concerns technical approaches to making AI safe, with Constitutional AI as the comparison.
The wording does not define whether an idea is a broad research family, a particular algorithm, or a proposal for comprehensive safety.
A research inventory can establish that alternatives existed, but cannot fairly turn few into a pass/fail count without adding a consequential counting rule.
The implied historical reference is October 2023, but no stable grading criterion follows from it.
criteria.support_condition: No non-arbitrary support condition can be specified without defining the eligible approaches, their level of distinctness, and what count qualifies as few.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No non-arbitrary contradiction condition can be specified from the wording alone. Listing papers does not establish how many distinct ideas the speaker meant.
